learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the core Keynesian model of how Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply determine the equilibrium level of income and employment in a nation.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: AD is the total demand for all final goods and services in an economy. In a two-sector model, AD = C (Consumption) + I (Investment).
MPC is the ratio of change in consumption to change in income (∆C/∆Y). It shows how much of an additional rupee earned gets spent. APC is Total Consumption divided by Total Income.
The economy is in equilibrium when Aggregate Demand equals Aggregate Supply (AD = AS), which is also the point where Planned Savings equals Planned Investment (S = I).

When new investment is made, it generates income. That income is spent (consumption), generating more income for others. The total increase in national income is a multiple of the initial investment. Multiplier (k) = 1 / (1 - MPC).

fun_activity.title: 💸 The Spending Chain
fun_activity.instructions: If the government builds a ₹100 crore bridge, they pay workers. The workers spend ₹80 crore on food and clothes (MPC = 0.8). The shopkeepers then spend ₹64 crore on other things. The initial ₹100 crore ripples through the economy, generating ₹500 crore in total income!

exam_tips: 📌 MPC + MPS = 1 always. If you know one, you can easily find the other.
📌 Be clear on the difference between 'Ex-ante' (planned) and 'Ex-post' (actual) investment/savings.
📌 Deficient demand leads to a 'Deflationary Gap', while excess demand leads to an 'Inflationary Gap'.
quick_recap: ⭐ Autonomous consumption is the minimum level of consumption that happens even when income is zero (funded by past savings or borrowing).
⭐ The investment multiplier works in both forward (increasing income) and backward (decreasing income) directions.
⭐ The government uses fiscal policy (taxes and spending) to correct excess or deficient demand.
